input.quote: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice. Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection.
input.rationale: Section 4.4 is the only audit/inspection right binding Corio (books and records supporting amounts payable to Commerce One); no other verification or systems-access right exists in the Agreement or Exhibits. The clause already limits inspections to once each calendar year, uses an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to Corio, and places costs on Commerce One, and it gives no direct access to Corio systems. It fails the fallback on two material terms: notice is only "reasonable notice" rather than a fixed minimum period, and the cost-shifting trigger is an underpayment of more than 5% rather than the 10% fallback threshold. We therefore fixed notice at fifteen (15) days and moved the reimbursement trigger to more than ten percent (10%), leaving the rest of the clause untouched. Preferred-level extras (30 days' notice, express business-hours and confidentiality wording, off-site where possible) are noted but not pursued given the clause otherwise sits at or above the fallback.

proposal.summary: Fix audit notice period and underpayment cost-shifting threshold in Section 4.4
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We can accept an annual records inspection, but we need a fixed notice period rather than "reasonable notice", so we have set at least fifteen (15) days. We have also aligned the cost-shifting trigger with our position that Commerce One bears the cost of the inspection unless it reveals an underpayment of more than ten percent (10%).
